newsitem.title: USA: SBC sees merger charges of $1.9-$2.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: SBC sees merger charges of $1.9-$2.3 bln.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc. said Thursday it expects to record one-time fiscal 1997 charges of $1.9-$2.3 billion as a result of its $16.5 billion merger with Pacific Telesis Group.

In a press release, the regional Bell operator said the charges stem from strategic decisions it has made pertaining to the merger, which closed April 1. It said $1.6-$1.9 billion of the charges will be recorded in the second quarter.

SBC also said it expects to incur additional pre-tax capital costs and expenses of $1.5 billion associated with the implementation of phone number portability for customers switching to new local phone service competitors.
It identified three sources for the one-time charges:
-- merger integration, which includes operations consolidations and job reductions;
-- scaling back of investment in video services and the halting of construction of a hybrid fiber-coaxial network in California;
-- actions by regulators during their review of the merger.
SBC said its restructuring decisions may add up to $1 billion annually to net income by the year 2000.
